newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Sterling joins yen in focus on Hungary FX futures.
newsitem.headline: Sterling joins yen in focus on Hungary FX futures.

text.p: Sterling shared the limelight with the yen on Hungary's forex futures market on Wednesday as the U.K. unit saw strong gains abroad, dealers said.
The yen and sterling accounted for two-thirds of all turnover on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) financial section, which saw a modest 3.68 billion forints turnover.
The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) saw a tiny six million forints' trade.
Sterling's strong spot performance on Wednesday triggered interest in short term maturities, with April, which saw substantial trade, rising one forint to 288.5 forints.
All other turnover was in longer-term maturities in currencies which offer low interest rates with which to speculate on the crawling peg devaluation of the forint.
Notable examples were September yen, which fell 70 fillers to 156.2 forints per 100 yen and the December mark, which fell 15 fillers to 116.16.
The forint is devalued by 1.2 percent per month against a central bank currency basket made up 70 percent of the mark and 30 percent of the dollar. The rate will change to 1.1 percent from April 1.
Wednesday's central bank midday fix was 142.40 per 100 yen, down 0.72, while sterling was fixed at 286.64, up 1.25, and the mark was 104.78, down 0.05.
The BSE saw one price change, a 30 filler rise in the March 1998 mark.
